rows.item: Descent module of Soyuz 27 (Soyuz 7K-T, flew to Salyut 6, 1978)
rows.notes: Type is 7K-T, which has no Orrery entry; mapped to nearest Soyuz crewed entry, operator to remap. Commons caption 'Спускаємий модуль Союза 27 (справжній)' = genuine; ru and en Wikipedia museum articles also say the flown Soyuz-27 descent module is displayed. Museum site cosmosmuseum.info did not give an exhibit page. Museum's Vostok and Vega descent apparatus items not clearly real, not recorded.

rows.item: Return capsule of Soyuz 28 (Remek/Gubarev, 1978) plus Remek's spacesuit
rows.notes: Soyuz 7K-T; mapped to nearest Orrery Soyuz entry. Wikipedia (cs, en) and Commons category 'Soyuz 28 at the Prague Aviation Museum' only; vhu.cz pages fetched do not mention it. Suit not matched to an Orrery suit.

rows.item: Original descent module of Soyuz 33 (Rukavishnikov/Ivanov, 1979), with Ivanov's suit and parachute
rows.notes: Soyuz 7K-T; mapped to nearest Orrery Soyuz entry. Museum's own cosmonautics collection page calls it the original descent module.
Soyuz 7K-T; mapped to nearest Orrery Soyuz entry. Article says original, transferred to museum 12 Feb 1982, visitors can see it; museum's own page not found (article is third party).

rows.item: Descent capsule of Soyuz 30 (Klimuk/Hermaszewski, 1978), with Hermaszewski's suits
rows.notes: Soyuz 7K-T; mapped to nearest Orrery Soyuz entry. Wikipedia and Commons photos (2013/2014) only; pl Wikipedia says Fort IX Czerniaków branch, another Wikipedia article says the main Polish Army Museum building. Current location not confirmed on a museum page.

rows.notes: Commons caption only ('pre-flight test unit'); other sources call it a test model, so real versus mock-up unresolved.
